title: Learning: The Liar
text: Until now nodes failed by stopping or falling behind. Now one may be sending different things to different nodes.
held: This time everyone was told the same story. With three nodes, that is luck, not protection.

cards.label: Refuse it and raise the alarm
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: what B was sent
fields.check: Compare notes with the other follower
fields.ok: B was sent the same entry.

intrusion.value: pay 900 to Okafor, at the same index
intrusion.detail: B was sent a different entry for index 12.
intrusion.correct: Refuse it and raise the alarm
intrusion.why: One node telling two stories is equivocation. Protocols built for crashes assume it never happens, and break when it does.
intrusion.reveal: The Leader sent two different entries for the same index.

temptations.label: Go with whichever version arrived first
temptations.why: First to arrive differs from node to node. That rule gives each follower a different log.

cards.label: Do not accept it
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: confirmed by
fields.check: Ask a second node to confirm the result
fields.ok: A second node reports the same result.

intrusion.why: If a node may lie, one node's word proves nothing. You need matching answers from more nodes than could be lying, and the cluster needs 3f + 1 nodes to tolerate f liars.
intrusion.reveal: Only the node that answered could confirm its own result.

teaches: Crash-tolerant consensus (three nodes for one failure) assumes nodes are honest when they speak.
Tolerating f lying nodes takes 3f + 1 nodes and signed messages. Three nodes cannot survive one liar.
discussion: Which systems you rely on assume honest nodes, and what would have to be true for that assumption to fail?
